what: Photos bend vertically like a bow by the scroll speed — the center is pushed further than the top and bottom edges, so scrolling fast makes them convex and stopping straightens them. One three canvas fixed to the screen lays a 10×10 cell plane under each photo and follows the element position every frame (the bend = cos(x·π) × .01 × speed × .07). Nothing is drawn beyond 10% above or below the screen

options.amp: Horizontal wave amplitude, default .1 (no wave if wavelength is 0)
options.freq: Horizontal wave length (multiplied by speed), default 0
options.pad: Extra amount drawn above and below the screen (ratio of screen height), default .1
options.img: If the element contains an img, draw that image, otherwise draw a placeholder panel using data-label

use: — call three first (if it is three.cjs, put three-global.js from this folder before it). If window.lenis exists, its speed is used
note: The original passes Lenis velocity straight through as uVelocity (px per frame). Without Lenis, the scroll difference between frames is used. It is not applied on touch devices (hover is false) or with reduced motion, so the DOM photos show as they are (the original also turns off WebGL on touch). The canvas covers the screen at z-index 3 but clicks pass through.

from.where: about.html .hs-ph (seven history photos — original history data-history-image, three r180)
